sources.title: Rieder et al. (1995): The checkpoint delaying anaphase in response to chromosome monoorientation
sources.supports: Opened primary article: laser ablation experiments identify unattached kinetochores as the source of an anaphase-inhibitory signal in PtK1 mammalian cells.

sources.supports: Publisher/PMC open was blocked; the primary abstract was retrieved directly through Europe PMC REST and saved in evidence/division/primary-source-abstracts.json. Serial EM reconstructions show antiparallel interdigitating populations, rather than a single strand spanning both poles. Detailed ipMT minus-end distributions are outside the schematic.

sources.title: Mouse Genetics: The mouse karyotype
sources.supports: Opened JAX scientific resource: standard mouse autosomes are telocentric; species has 19 autosomal pairs, so the stated two-pair subset must not be read as a karyotype.

sources.title: Ogushi et al. (2021): Loss of sister kinetochore co-orientation and peri-centromeric cohesin protection
sources.supports: Opened primary abstract and figure captions: co-orientation and pericentromeric cohesion preserve sisters through I; loss in II permits sister disjunction. The experiment uses mouse oocytes; used only for conserved chromosome mechanics, not male-specific cytokinesis.

sources.title: Greenbaum et al. (2006): TEX14 is essential for intercellular bridges and fertility in male mice
sources.supports: Primary abstract retrieved through Europe PMC REST after PMC/PubMed opens were blocked; saved locally. Mouse germ-cell cytokinesis retains permanent cytoplasmic channels; loss of TEX14 eliminates bridges.

sources.title: Delivery of ceramide phosphoethanolamine lipids to the cleavage furrow through the endocytic pathway is essential for male meiotic cytokinesis (2022)
sources.supports: Opened primary article, Figure 4 and associated live-imaging results: normal actomyosin ring/furrow constriction remains coupled; membrane detachment accompanies failed cytokinesis. Drosophila experiments support the generic coupling invariant only; no insect lipid/mutant mechanism is transferred to the mouse model.

findings.evidence: Three existing actomyosin belts retain the old independent scale formulas although the membrane now deforms as a joined-lobe level set. At p=0.495, actual first-ring centreline samples lie 0.38679, 0.41958 and 0.51766 world units from the inner membrane triangles. At p=0.865, both second-ring samples are 0.34319-0.44434 units away. Sampling uses world-transformed ring centreline and nearest triangle surfaces at negative-z positions retained in the cutaway, so this is not a front-cut or nearest-vertex artifact. Full bounded records: evidence/division/diagnostics.json, ringContacts.
findings.whyWrong: The normal dividing-cell scene depicts a contractile belt shrinking deep inside the cytoplasm while the membrane remains distant, breaking the mechanical attachment responsible for furrow ingression. The gap greatly exceeds the tube radius (~0.013 times ring scale), and is sustained through both constrictions.
findings.fix: Drive each belt from the actual level-set cleavage cross-section or deform membrane and belt from a shared geometric contour; keep a cortical inset consistent with leaflet/ring thickness, preserve retained open bridges, and preserve the full chromosome and membrane detail.
findings.verification: During both division windows, test several actual rear belt vertices/centreline points against transformed inner-membrane triangles across early, middle and late contraction; require a bounded cortical gap that rejects the present 0.34-0.52 displacement. Retain membrane lumen/manifold and irregular seek/resource tests.

findings.evidence: A bounded same-process diagnostic measured 12 changing-membrane poses p=.480-.491 after warmup: median update 32.6759 ms, max 53.8420 ms; 12 stable-membrane poses p=.640-.651: median 0.2972 ms, max 0.3925 ms. The moving path recomputes 70,395 scalar samples, finite-difference gradients and two full 64x56x18 marching-tetrahedron scans synchronously. Timing data saved in evidence/division/diagnostics.json.
findings.whyWrong: The changing-membrane update alone exceeds a 16.7 ms frame budget before rendering on the audit host, placing continuous constriction playback at risk even though absolute seeking succeeds. This confirms excessive synchronous work at these measured poses, not a claimed browser FPS measurement.
findings.fix: Optimize repeated work while retaining identical grid resolution, isosurface detail, bridge topology, absolute seeking and stable geometry/material/node identities; favor cached grid topology, active-cell reuse within one update, bounded updates and exact arithmetic reuse over reducing resolution.
findings.verification: Repeat the same bounded moving/stable samples and compare actual output geometry/topology with the baseline. Root must separately measure rendered playback at both changing-membrane intervals; current concurrent host load limits precise performance attribution.

continuity.checked: Paired/crossed, I segregation, rotation, II segregation, nuclear reassembly, all membrane-changing intervals and visibility boundaries traced; 26 repeated irregular pose checks.
limits: No browser FPS or physical-device claim; numeric update timings were collected while other audit agents were active.
Spindle and synapsis visibility switches require root visual judgement; no extra defect assigned merely because a visibility flag changes.
Surface triangulation connectivity changes during division; index correspondence is not used as a false geometric-discontinuity metric.

limitations: Mouse-oocyte primary data supports chromosome-orientation mechanics only; male bridge scope is supported independently by mouse TEX14 study.
No full sexual chromosome behavior, recombination repair chemistry, sperm maturation or realistic meiotic timing is claimed.
Inherited bridges to other preexisting germ cells are outside the explicitly followed single-cell lineage.
Updated membrane geometry was measured; a passing former audit cannot certify the current belt attachment.
